subject: Eval access lanes kickoff + cleanroom cadence and close milestones
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@retailco.com>, Oliver Smith <oliver@marketplace.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval access lanes kickoff + cleanroom cadence and close milestones

Hi Elena / Oliver,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to kick off the mutual action plan for exchanging the evaluation materials (prompt pack + testcases + sample dataset) and to propose a tight cadence so we hit your November POC close window. High level asks:

- Redwood provides ephemeral sandbox access + prompt pack (attached) by 10/26.
- RetailCo supplies acceptance criteria set and a PO by 11/05.
- Takedown/destruction of ephemeral copies no later than 12/01 (unless extended by written agreement).

Key constraints we need to capture up-front:
- Dataset is provisioned for evaluation only; no model training or redistribution.
- Prompt pack and testcases are shared under ephemeral license: limited to named engineers and test runners listed in the MAP.
- Audit trail required: logs for model calls + token-level usage stored for 90 days.

I attached a working MAP draft (MAP-draft-RI-RetailCo.pdf), the prompt pack (retailco_promptpack_v1.zip) and a dataset manifest (dataset_manifest_v3.csv) so you can confirm there aren't any redlines on file-level constraints.

Can you confirm the acceptance gate you expect for the POC (e.g., top-line accuracy thresholds, safety checks), and whether the PO timeline above is workable? If so we'll spin up the sandbox + provide ephemeral credentials.

Next steps I propose:
1) Elena confirms acceptance gates and PO target date (reply by 10/23).
2) Redwood sends DocuSign MAP and provisioning link (by 10/24).
3) RetailCo signs MAP and returns PO (by 11/05).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to align on the access lanes and the cleanroom-style constraints before we provision anything.

Best,

David Kim
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: retailco_promptpack_v1.zip (prompt pack, 12 files), dataset_manifest_v3.csv (metadata), MAP-draft-RI-RetailCo.pdf (3 pages)
From: Elena Ortiz <elena@retailco.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval access lanes kickoff + cleanroom cadence and close milestones

David — thanks for the clear plan and materials. Quick responses inline: 

- Acceptance gate: we will measure on three fronts for the POC: accuracy on top-10 intents (target >= 86%), false-positive safety triggers below 2%, and latency 95p < 300ms in the sandbox. We'll formalize as a short acceptance doc and add to the MAP.
- PO timeline: 11/05 is fine; procurement needs the signed MAP + SOW to cut the PO.
- Usage constraints: RetailCo agrees to evaluation-only, no training. We need one clarification: can Redwood guarantee ephemeral tokens are disabled after the takedown date and provide a certificate of destruction? Procurement will ask for that.

Two small asks on the prompt pack: can you remove any examples that reference RetailCo PII (there were two customer-email samples in /examples) before we share with a wider engineering group? We can take that offline.

If you can send the DocuSign link today, procurement and legal will triage it and we should be able to return signatures within 48–72 hours.

Thanks — Elena
Head of Data Science, RetailCo

Elena — noted on the removal of PII examples; we'll sanitize the examples in the prompt pack and put a redacted copy in the Drive folder. I'll update the manifest to show which files were redacted.

On the certificate of destruction: Redwood can provide a takedown certificate summarizing the assets removed and the timestamp of token revocation. Our standard is to provide that within 5 business days of takedown. If Procurement needs a different SLA, let us know.

Operational notes for David / Ben:
- I'll prepare the DocuSign MAP with an explicit clause: \"ephemeral access tokens will be revoked and access lanes closed on the takedown date; Redwood will provide a takedown certificate within 5 business days.\"
- Sandbox provisioning: access lanes scoped to 6 named accounts (engineers & QA) and one service account for CI. Ephemeral credentials will be labeled with the MAP id.
- Audit logs: we'll share a read-only log export with RetailCo for the 90d retention window.

I'll upload the redacted prompt pack and updated manifest by EOD 10/22.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) We'll send the DocuSign link this morning. It will contain the MAP, a short SOW with the acceptance criteria you described, and the takedown/certificate language Marissa mentioned.
2) Redaction: Marissa will upload the sanitized prompt pack to the Drive link (I've added it to related_links).

Proposed provisioning timeline after signature:
- Day 0 (signature): create sandbox + invite named users (ephemeral tokens provisioned).
- Day 1: upload datasets and run smoke tests with RetailCo.
- Week 1–2: POC runs; we collect metrics and share daily dashboard.

I'll keep the thread updated when the DS link is live. Thanks for the quick turnaround — we'll aim to keep the MAP tight so procurement can cut the PO.
